summary: As of August 2026 the FRC autonomous stack has consolidated onto two interoperable tools plus a hand-rolled tier. PathPlanner 2026.1.2 (Jan 12 2026) is a GUI-first, spline-based planner whose 2025 ground-up rewrite replaced replanning/ReplanningConfig with a torque/friction-aware trajectory generator driven by RobotConfig (mass, MOI, module offsets, wheel COF, drive motor, current limit) and emits per-module DriveFeedforwards that feed straight into Phoenix 6's SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds.withWheelForceFeedforwardsX/Y; it uniquely owns on-the-fly pathfinding (AD*/LocalADStar over deploy/pathplanner/navgrid.json) via AutoBuilder.pathfindToPose / pathfindThenFollowPath. Choreo 2026 (v2026.0.3, Apr 6 2026) is a time-optimal numerical optimizer (TrajoptLib on Sleipnir) that produces pre-baked .traj files and, critically, ships ChoreoLib's AutoFactory/AutoRoutine/AutoTrajectory — a trigger-based composition API (atTime, atTimeBeforeEnd, atTranslation, atPose, done, doneDelayed, recentlyDone, anyDone, anyActive) that is strictly more expressive for mechanism coordination than PathPlanner's NamedCommands, and it cannot regenerate from the robot's actual starting state. The two are complementary, not competing: PathPlannerPath.fromChoreoTrajectory(name, splitIndex) lets PPLib follow Choreo output, and PathPlannerAuto now exposes the same trigger surface (event, beforeEvent, distanceFromEvent, nearFieldPositionAutoFlipped, inFieldAreaAutoFlipped, timeRange, condition) plus a mirror constructor. Elite teams do not use either library's auto files as the top-level structure: 6328's 2026 code loads Choreo Trajectory<SwerveSample> but follows it with a custom DriveTrajectory command (3 PIDs + trajectory feedforward + an omega override for shoot-on-the-move) and composes autos from question-driven AutoSelector responses; 254's 2025 auto was fully dynamic — a scoring-sequence string from a custom dashboard driving AD* pathfinding with per-phase navgrids, retry-on-failed-intake, and a 12-second "skip to starred step" budget; 1678's 2026 code uses ChoreoLib AutoFactory with factory.bind() global event markers plus an AutoModeBase wrapper adding mirroring and collision detection; 2910 uses Choreo.TrajectoryCache with a Superstructure state enum. The genuine gaps PumpkinLib should fill are (a) a single trigger/composition surface that works identically over PathPlanner and Choreo trajectories, (b) a superstructure request bus with graph-search transitions (254 ships an AStarSolver over superstructure states), (c) a headless auto validation harness that replays every auto variant in maple-sim and asserts a timing budget, and (d) an auto-chooser with dependent questions. WPILib 2027 is a hard break — Systemcore, Java 25, org.wpilib packages, Commands v3 coroutines, Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/PathWeaver/RobotBuilder removed — so any PumpkinLib auto API must be a thin facade over the command framework, not a fork of it.

landscape.doesWell: GUI path+auto editor with waypoints, rotation targets, constraint zones, point-towards zones, and zoned/non-zoned event markers. AutoBuilder.configure(Supplier<Pose2d> poseSupplier, Consumer<Pose2d> resetPose, Supplier<ChassisSpeeds> robotRelativeSpeeds, BiConsumer<ChassisSpeeds,DriveFeedforwards> output, PathFollowingController, RobotConfig, BooleanSupplier shouldFlipPath, Subsystem... driveRequirements). Only mainstream lib with on-the-fly pathfinding: AutoBuilder.pathfindToPose(Pose2d, PathConstraints[, goalEndVelocity]), pathfindToPoseFlipped(...), pathfindThenFollowPath(PathPlannerPath, PathConstraints), backed by AD*/LocalADStar over deploy/pathplanner/navgrid.json. Regenerates trajectory from actual robot start state. RobotConfig.fromGUISettings() reads settings.json so mass/MOI/COF/motor/current-limit live in one place. Emits DriveFeedforwards (per-module force) that map 1:1 onto Phoenix 6 ApplyRobotSpeeds.withWheelForceFeedforwardsX/Y. Rich trigger API on PathPlannerAuto (event, beforeEvent, distanceFromEvent, distanceFromEventEnd, pointTowardsZone, activePath, nearFieldPosition(AutoFlipped), inFieldArea(AutoFlipped), timeElapsed, timeRange, condition, isRunning). SendableChooser generation via buildAutoChooser()/buildAutoChooserWithOptionsModifier(Function<Stream<PathPlannerAuto>,Stream<PathPlannerAuto>>). Ships SwerveSetpointGenerator (254-derived) and PPHolonomicDriveController with static feedback overrides (overrideXFeedback/overrideYFeedback/overrideXYFeedback/overrideRotationFeedback/clearFeedbackOverrides).
landscape.gaps: Trajectories are spline+profile, not time-optimal — measurably slower than Choreo on the same waypoints for aggressive autos. NamedCommands is a global string->Command registry, which is a hidden-coupling footgun (a NamedCommand sharing requirements with the auto group cancels the group). No first-class branching inside an .auto file — dynamic autos must be built in Java, abandoning the GUI. Event markers are the only in-path coordination primitive at the .auto level; the richer trigger API only exists once you wrap in PathPlannerAuto in Java. Pathfinding is non-deterministic under AdvantageKit replay unless you swap in LocalADStarAK. Choreo trajectories loaded via fromChoreoTrajectory cannot be regenerated to match actual start state.
landscape.version2026: PathPlanner 2026.1.2, released 2026-01-12 (2026.1.1 on 2026-01-11 was the first 2026-season stable, adding the REBUILT field image and PPLibTesting.resetForTesting()). Per release notes 2026 had no major API changes over 2025; the 2025 release was the ground-up trajectory generation rewrite.
landscape.integrationShape:
RobotConfig cfg = RobotConfig.fromGUISettings();
AutoBuilder.configure(
    robotState::getPose,
    robotState::resetPose,
    drive::getRobotRelativeSpeeds,
    (speeds, ff) -> drive.setControl(
        applyRobotSpeeds.withSpeeds(speeds)
            .withWheelForceFeedforwardsX(ff.robotRelativeForcesXNewtons())
            .withWheelForceFeedforwardsY(ff.robotRelativeForcesYNewtons())),
    new PPHolonomicDriveController(new PIDConstants(5,0,0), new PIDConstants(5,0,0)),
    cfg,
    () -> DriverStation.getAlliance().orElse(Alliance.Blue) == Alliance.Red,
    drive);
NamedCommands.registerCommands(Map.of("intake", superstructure.request(INTAKE), "score", superstructure.request(SCORE_L4)));
Pathfinding.setPathfinder(new LocalADStarAK()); // AdvantageKit users, before warmup
FollowPathCommand.warmupCommand().schedule();   // in robotInit

landscape.doesWell: Time-optimal trajectory optimization respecting real dynamics constraints; faster wall-clock autos than spline-and-profile for the same waypoints. Constraint set: Stop Point, Max Velocity, Max Acceleration, Max Angular Velocity, Point At, Keep In Circle/Rectangle/Lane, Keep Out Circle, applied at waypoint scope, segment scope, or both. Waypoint types: Pose (translation+rotation), Translation, Empty (cannot be an endpoint). AutoFactory/AutoRoutine/AutoTrajectory give the best-in-class mechanism-coordination surface in FRC: AutoTrajectory exposes active(), inactive(), done(), doneDelayed(double), doneFor(double), recentlyDone(), atTime(double), atTime(String eventName), atTimeBeforeEnd(double), atTranslation(Translation2d|String, tol), atPose(Pose2d|String, transTol, rotTol), collectEventTimes(String), collectEventPoses(String), chain(AutoTrajectory), spawnCmd(), resetOdometry(), getInitialPose()/getFinalPose(), and mirrorX()/mirrorY()/rotateAround(). AutoRoutine adds anyActive(...), allInactive(...), anyDone(...), anyDoneDelayed(int cycles, ...), observe(BooleanSupplier), cmd(), cmd(BooleanSupplier finish), idle(), kill(), reset(), poll(), loop(). AutoChooser does lazy generation: addRoutine(String, Supplier<AutoRoutine>), addCmd(String, Supplier<Command>), selectedCommandScheduler(). Split waypoints let one .traj be addressed as sub-trajectories by index. Generated Java files from the GUI have no ChoreoLib dependency.
landscape.gaps: No pathfinding / on-the-fly path generation whatsoever — everything is pre-baked. No ability to regenerate from actual start state, so a bumped start pose means the follower fights a stale feedforward. Choreo does not support PathPlanner-style zoned events (markers are instants only). Optimizer failures are opaque to students; solve times can be long and require regeneration on every robot-config change. No GUI-level auto sequencing at all — composition is 100% Java. .traj loading is blocking and must happen at startup.
landscape.version2026: Choreo v2026.0.3 (2026-04-06). 2026.0.0 was the season release; 2026.0.1 (2026-01-12) was macOS/vendordep fixes with ChoreoLib unchanged; 2026.0.2 (2026-03-02) moved Java codegen to the backend enabling CLI codegen and added an alliance-flipped trajectory view; 2026.0.3 added mirrorX()/mirrorY()/rotateAround() trajectory flipping, a Java warmup command, and solver angular-acceleration handling in the swerve equation (Sleipnir 0.5.1). Vendordep: https://choreo.autos/lib/ChoreoLib2026.json

landscape.doesWell: Command composition primitives every auto architecture is built on: Commands.sequence/parallel/deadline/race/either/select/repeatingSequence/waitUntil/waitSeconds/runOnce/defer/print, Command.withTimeout/raceWith/deadlineFor/alongWith/andThen/finallyDo, Trigger + EventLoop (which ChoreoLib's AutoRoutine is built on), RobotModeTriggers.autonomous(), SendableChooser, ProfiledPIDController, TrapezoidProfile, HolonomicDriveController, LTVUnicycleController (used by ChoreoLib's differential example), SwerveDriveKinematics, SwerveDrivePoseEstimator.
landscape.gaps: No opinionated auto architecture, no auto-selector-with-questions, no timing budget tooling, no trajectory abstraction shared across vendors. Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard are deprecated targets going into 2027.
landscape.version2026: WPILib 2026.x on roboRIO/Java 17. WPILib 2027 is a hard break: Systemcore replaces roboRIO, Java 25 / C++23 required, packages move edu.wpi.first -> org.wpilib (frc:: -> wpi::), Commands v3 (coroutine-based, compile-time checks for unsafe coroutine usage, rising/falling edge trigger factories, declarative state machine API) added alongside a pruned Commands v2 (RamseteCommand and controller-based commands removed), Shuffleboard + SmartDashboard + PathWeaver + RobotBuilder removed (Choreo named PathWeaver's successor), kinematics made immutable, geometry classes final, trajectory APIs cleaned up with motion profile state structs, pose estimator gains acceleration support, all 2026 projects must be re-imported.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should depend only on the command primitives and Trigger/EventLoop, exposing its own PumpkinTrajectory/PumpkinAuto types so the 2027 org.wpilib + Commands v3 migration is a single internal adapter swap rather than a user-code rewrite.

landscape.doesWell: Deterministic log replay of the full robot-code state, which is the single highest-leverage auto-debugging tool that exists: a failed auto at an event can be replayed offline with added logging. LoggedDashboardChooser is the de-facto auto chooser for AK teams (used by 254 and 6328). Logger.recordOutput of trajectory poses feeds AdvantageScope 2D/3D field views.
landscape.gaps: Pathfinding, RNG, and any non-deterministic data source break replay unless wrapped — PathPlanner's LocalADStar specifically must be replaced with LocalADStarAK (mjansen4857 gist) or replay diverges. No built-in auto-validation harness.
landscape.version2026: AdvantageKit 2026 ("Replay, Refined"); 5th season. UNVERIFIED: exact 2026 version number and whether LocalADStarAK is now shipped in-tree rather than as a gist — the gist remains the linked source from PathPlanner docs.

landscape.doesWell: Physics-engine (dyn4j) simulation of the drivetrain interacting with the field: game pieces, walls, other robots, wheel friction/slip. Makes autos testable without a field — the intended use case includes validating autonomous modes and pathfinding auto-align. Ships AdvantageKit Spark and TalonFX swerve templates with maple-sim already wired.
landscape.gaps: Simulated COF/mass/MOI still have to be measured to be meaningful; sim success does not validate vision-based pose correction or real intake reliability. Not an official WPILib project, so 2027/Systemcore support is a schedule risk.
landscape.version2026: Supports FRC 2026 "REBUILT" field/game pieces on WPILib 2026.2.1.

landscape.doesWell: SwerveDrivetrain + SwerveRequest give a tuned, high-rate (odometry thread) drive that both PathPlanner and Choreo plug into. SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds accepts per-module wheel force feedforwards in newtons: WheelForceFeedforwardsX (forward, +X) and WheelForceFeedforwardsY (leftward, +Y), array order matching module order — exactly the shape PathPlanner's DriveFeedforwards and Choreo's SwerveSample force fields (fx/fy per module) emit.
landscape.gaps: ApplyRobotSpeeds does NOT discretize speeds for you — the caller must. ApplyChassisSpeeds was renamed to ApplyRobotSpeeds and the old name is deprecated for removal in 2026. Tuner X constants and PathPlanner settings.json are two separate sources of truth for mass/MOI/wheel radius, which drift apart.
landscape.version2026: Phoenix 6 26.1.1 (Java API docs marked 26.1.1 stable as of Aug 2026).

landscape.doesWell: Demonstrates the fully-dynamic auto: AutoModeSelector offers only DO_NOTHING and CUSTOM, where CUSTOM is parameterized by start position (LEFT/MIDDLE/RIGHT), ice-cream count (0-3), feeder strategy (GROUND/FUNNEL), and a scoring-sequence string + level-sequence string read from NetworkTables. PathfindingAuto walks those strings, calling AutoFactory.getPathfindToReefCommand(...) per step. Vendored PathPlannerLib under com.team254.lib.pathplanner so they could add PPHolonomicDriveController.setControlPoint(Transform2d) (offsetting the controlled point to the scoring mechanism rather than robot center) and multiple navgrids (navgrid.json, auto_navgrid.json, backoff_navgrid.json) swapped at runtime via Pathfinding.setBackoffObstacles()/setTeleopObstacles(). Superstructure is a SuperstructureStateMachine over SuperstructureState with a generic AStarSolver<N>.solve(N start, N goal, Heuristic<N>, Neighbors<N>) finding minimum-cost legal transition chains, plus CoralStateTracker and ModalSuperstructureTriggers.setFutureStateAndWaitUntilDesiredCommand(state, ...). Retry logic: on failed intake, decrement currentStep and set retrying=true. Timing budget: past 12s of auto, jump to the next '*'-marked step in the level sequence.
landscape.gaps: Vendoring PathPlannerLib means manual re-merge every season. Extremely team-specific; nothing reusable is packaged.
landscape.version2026: UNVERIFIED — no public Team254 FRC-2026 repo was located in this pass; 2025 is the latest public release found.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib equivalent: PumpkinSuperstructure.graph(State.class).edge(A, B, cost, guard, action) + .requestAsync(goal) returning a Command that A*-searches the transition graph; and PumpkinAuto.dynamic(Supplier<List<AutoStep>>) that rebuilds the step list each cycle from dashboard/vision state.

landscape.doesWell: Loads Choreo Trajectory<SwerveSample> via Choreo.loadTrajectory(name) but follows with its own DriveTrajectory extends Command: x/y PIDController(linearkP,0,linearkD,0.02) + thetaController with enableContinuousInput(-pi,pi), sampling trajectory.sampleAt(timer.get(), shouldFlip()) and adding sample feedforward velocities, finishing at trajectory.getTotalTime(). Constructor takes (Trajectory<SwerveSample>, Supplier<Optional<Double>> omegaOverride, Drive, BooleanSupplier mirror) — the omega override is how shoot-on-the-move works during a path (launchOnTheMoveOmega()). AutoSelector extends VirtualSubsystem with addRoutine(String name, List<AutoQuestion> questions, Command command) where AutoQuestion is a record(String question, List<AutoQuestionResponse> responses), publishing up to 6 dependent question dropdowns to NetworkTables and freezing responses once auto is enabled. AutoCommands.java shows dynamic composition: Commands.repeatingSequence of intake/return/fire cycles, .raceWith(Commands.waitUntil(() -> withinTolerance(pose, 0.25, rot))) to time mechanism actions against pose rather than time, SalesmanSolver (TSP over detected game pieces) and getDynamicBounds() that expands the search region based on ObjectDetection.getInstance().getRobotTranslations() (opponent robots seen by vision). SimTrajectory(String name, FuelSim fuelSim, int instance, BooleanSupplier isBlueAlliance, BooleanSupplier mirror) replays an auto against a fuel/game-piece simulation to score autos without a field. DriveToPose(Drive, Supplier<Pose2d> target, Supplier<Optional<Double>> omegaOverride) uses ProfiledPIDController with continuous input, ~14 LoggedTunableNumbers, and linear/theta feedforward scalers clamped 0..1 by (error - ffMin)/(ffMax - ffMin) to blend profile FF out near the goal; exposes withinTolerance(double driveTolerance, Rotation2d thetaTolerance). DriveCommands.feedforwardCharacterization does a 0.1 V/s ramp with a closed-form least-squares kS/kV fit; wheelRadiusCharacterization spins at a SlewRateLimiter(0.05)-limited 0.25 rad/s and computes wheelRadius = (gyroDelta * driveBaseRadius) / wheelDelta.
landscape.gaps: Entirely bespoke; nothing packaged for reuse. Trajectories come from an internal generation service (src/main/deploy/vts/*.traj) rather than the Choreo GUI in the general case.
landscape.version2026: 2026 season code, public mirror updated from their internal repo.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib equivalents worth copying wholesale: PumpkinDriveToPose (ProfiledPID + FF blend + withinTolerance), PumpkinCharacterization.feedforward(drive) and .wheelRadius(drive), PumpkinAutoSelector.addRoutine(name, List<Question>, Command).

landscape.doesWell: Cleanest published 2026 example of ChoreoLib at scale. AutoModeBase wraps an AutoRoutine created by factory.newRoutine(name) and re-exposes trajectory(String), trajectory(String,int splitIndex), trajectory(Trajectory<SampleType>), prepRoutine(Command... steps), getRoutine(), asCommand(), plus midline-mirroring, bump traversal with pitch monitoring, collision detection, and vision-based pose correction. AutoHelpers.bindEventMarkers() registers global Choreo markers: "intake" deploys intake + roller speeds, "spinUp" sets 1900 RPM and 19.5 deg hood, "expandHopper" moves the climber. Other helpers: waitForAutoAlignedOrTimeout(), fireCommand() (parallel spinup + hopper contraction timing + post-fire stow), fireCommandWithoutDrop(), resetPoseIfWithoutEstimate(), isInsideNeutralZone(). Auto modes are individual classes under autos/midline/ and autos/midline/single/ (LeftSingleSweep, RightSingleSweep), each extending AutoModeBase — a class-per-auto pattern that makes dozens of variants tractable.
landscape.gaps: Team-specific superstructure coupling; no library extraction.
landscape.version2026: 2026 season. vendordeps: ChoreoLib2026.json, Phoenix6-frc2026-latest.json, WPILibNewCommands.json, photonlib-v2026.1.1-rc-3.json. deploy/choreo/comp.chor plus per-segment .traj files.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should ship exactly this shape as a base class: public abstract class PumpkinAutoMode { protected PumpkinTrajectory traj(String name); protected PumpkinTrajectory traj(String name, int split); protected abstract void define(); public Command asCommand(); }

landscape.doesWell: Straightforward, teachable structure: autos/ contains Auto, AutoChooser, AutoFactory, AutoProgram, Location; subsystems/Superstructure.java holds a WantedSuperState enum. Composition is Commands.sequence(followThenScore(ReefFaces.AB, SCORE_LEFT_L4), followThenIntakeFromStation(...), ...). Trajectories load via Choreo.TrajectoryCache; DeferredCommand is used where the target pose is only known at runtime. Both alliance variants are stored as separate pre-generated .traj files (BLUE_*/RED_*) rather than being flipped at runtime.
landscape.gaps: Duplicating every trajectory per alliance doubles the regeneration burden and is strictly worse than runtime flipping/mirroring now that Choreo 2026 has mirrorX/mirrorY and PathPlannerAuto has a mirror constructor.
landscape.version2026: 2025 season code (REEFSCAPE). UNVERIFIED: no 2026 public repo located in this pass.
landscape.integrationShape: Anti-pattern to design against: PumpkinLib's PumpkinTrajectory must make alliance handling a single flag (flip = mirror about field center for rotationally-symmetric fields, mirrorX/mirrorY for reflected fields) so teams never duplicate .traj files.

landscape.doesWell: UNVERIFIED for this domain in this pass.
landscape.gaps: 971's competition code is primarily C++/Rust with a bespoke spline planner and was not fetched here; FRC3476's GitHub org shows no 2026 robot repo (latest robot code is FRC-2025, last updated 2025-11-29), so no 2026 auto architecture claims can be made about either.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinTrajectory — one trigger/composition surface over BOTH PathPlanner and Choreo
capabilities.whyItMatters: This is the single biggest lever and it genuinely does not exist. Today a team must pick a library and then write all of its auto logic against that library's trigger vocabulary; switching (or mixing a Choreo sprint with a PathPlanner pathfind-to-reef) means rewriting the auto. The two vocabularies are already ~90% isomorphic (PathPlannerAuto.event/beforeEvent/distanceFromEvent/nearFieldPosition/timeRange vs AutoTrajectory.atTime/atTimeBeforeEnd/atTranslation/atPose/done), so a thin adapter is honest, small, and immediately buys a small team the ability to use Choreo where speed matters and PathPlanner pathfinding where the field is dynamic — without two codebases.
capabilities.prerequisites: PathPlannerLib 2026.x and ChoreoLib2026 both as compileOnly/optional Gradle deps so a team that installs only one still compiles; a PumpkinTrajectorySource SPI so custom trajectory formats (6328-style .traj from your own generator) can be plugged in. Requires PathPlannerPath.getIdealTrajectory(RobotConfig) for time math on the PP side.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAutoRoutine — declarative auto DSL with per-step timing budgets and fallbacks
capabilities.whyItMatters: Small teams lose autos to two things: no timeout anywhere, and a step that silently fails leaving the robot parked. 254 handles this by decrementing the step index and retrying, plus a hard 12s cutoff that skips to the next starred step; 6328 handles it with .raceWith(Commands.waitUntil(...)) and withTimeout. Neither is packaged. Making budgets and fallbacks a first-class part of the DSL means a novice team gets 254's failure discipline by default instead of by accident.
capabilities.apiSketch:
PumpkinAuto auto = PumpkinAuto.named("3pc Left")
  .startAt(traj1)                       // resetOdometry from traj1 initial pose
  .step(s -> s.follow(traj1)
              .with(superstructure.request(INTAKE))          // parallel, ends with the step
              .before(0.30, superstructure.request(SCORE_READY)) // atTimeBeforeEnd
              .budget(Seconds.of(3.2))                        // logs overrun, does not kill
              .deadline(Seconds.of(4.5)))                     // hard cutoff
  .step(s -> s.score(superstructure.scoreAndWait(L4)).timeout(Seconds.of(1.0)))
  .branch(sensors::hasPiece,
          ifTrue  -> ifTrue.step(s -> s.follow(traj2)),
          ifFalse -> ifFalse.step(s -> s.follow(retryTraj)).retry(1))
  .fallbackAfter(Seconds.of(12.0), auto -> auto.skipTo("park"))
  .build();
// build() returns a plain Command; every step publishes
// Auto/Steps/<i>/{name,plannedSeconds,actualSeconds,overrun,completed} for post-match triage.
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinTrajectory; a logging sink (AdvantageKit Logger.recordOutput or WPILog DataLog) injected rather than hard-depended-on.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinSuperstructure — request bus + transition graph with A* pathing between states
capabilities.whyItMatters: "Drive here while raising the elevator, score at the end" only works if the mechanism side is a single asynchronous request target, not N subsystems each grabbed by a command group. Requirement collisions between an auto group and an event-marker command are PathPlanner's documented #1 footgun (a NamedCommand sharing requirements cancels the auto group). 254 solved this with a SuperstructureStateMachine plus a generic AStarSolver over legal state transitions; 2910 and 1678 with a WantedSuperState enum. A small team cannot build this in-season, but can consume it.
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinLib's mechanism/subsystem abstraction (the "mechanisms easy to create and modify" goal) must land first — the state graph needs a uniform way to express a mechanism goal. Depends on the PID-tuning module for per-mechanism gains.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinDriveToPose — ProfiledPID pose alignment with feedforward blending and tolerance triggers
capabilities.whyItMatters: Scoring alignment is where small teams bleed cycles. 6328's DriveToPose is the reference implementation and is copy-pasted around the community every year, but nobody packages it. Bundling it with the pathfinding handoff (pathfind coarse, DriveToPose fine) gives a small team elite-grade alignment in one line.
capabilities.apiSketch:
Command align = PumpkinDriveToPose.builder(drive, robotState::getPose)
    .target(() -> FieldPoses.nearestReefBranch(robotState.getPose()))
    .constraints(MetersPerSecond.of(3.0), MetersPerSecondPerSecond.of(4.0),
                 DegreesPerSecond.of(540), DegreesPerSecondPerSecond.of(720))
    .ffBlend(0.20, 0.80)          // linearFFMinRadius/MaxRadius (m): blend profile FF out near goal
    .thetaFfBlend(Degrees.of(8), Degrees.of(40))
    .omegaOverride(() -> aim.shootOnTheMoveOmega())   // optional, for score-on-the-move
    .controlPointOffset(new Transform2d(0.35, 0, Rotation2d.kZero)) // 254 pattern: control the
                                                                    // mechanism, not robot center
    .tolerance(Meters.of(0.02), Degrees.of(1.0))
    .build();
Trigger aligned = PumpkinDriveToPose.atGoal(align);
// Coarse+fine composition:
Command go = PumpkinNav.pathfindTo(pose, constraints).andThen(align);
capabilities.prerequisites: Pose estimator handle (RobotState); PathPlannerLib for the pathfinding half of the handoff.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAutoSelector — dependent-question chooser with lazy generation and alliance mirroring
capabilities.whyItMatters: Dozens of auto variants is the elite pattern (6328 ships up to 6 dependent questions per routine; 254 ships a scoring-sequence string). A flat SendableChooser with 40 entries is unusable at an event and forces a rebuild per variant. Lazy generation (Choreo's AutoChooser.addRoutine(Supplier<AutoRoutine>)) plus dependent questions gives combinatorial coverage from a handful of building blocks, and freezing responses when auto is enabled prevents the classic mid-match dropdown disaster.
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinAutoRoutine; an Elastic/NT4-compatible dashboard widget spec, since Shuffleboard and SmartDashboard are removed in WPILib 2027.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAutoTest — headless auto validation harness with timing budget assertions
capabilities.whyItMatters: "How do you verify an auto works without a field" has no packaged answer today. 6328 built SimTrajectory + FuelSim internally to score autos in simulation; maple-sim provides the physics but no test harness. A JUnit-style harness that runs every registered auto variant headlessly against maple-sim, asserts it completes inside 15s (2026 auto period; confirm for 2027), asserts final pose, and reports per-step overrun would let a 10-person team validate 40 variants on a laptop overnight. This is the single highest-value thing PumpkinLib can build that nobody ships.
capabilities.prerequisites: maple-sim integration (thin-wrapper); PumpkinAutoRoutine step instrumentation; a headless CommandScheduler driver that can step faster than real time; WPILog writer for AdvantageScope playback.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinCharacterization — one-command feedforward, wheel radius, MOI, and COF measurement that writes RobotConfig/settings.json
capabilities.whyItMatters: PathPlanner's trajectory quality is a direct function of settings.json (mass, MOI, wheel radius, wheel COF, true max drive speed, drive current limit) and Choreo's optimizer depends on the same numbers; teams guess them, then blame the follower. 6328 ships both routines as ~40 lines each. Making measurement one dashboard button AND having it write back to the config file closes the loop nobody closes.
capabilities.apiSketch:
PumpkinCharacterization.feedforward(drive)      // 0.1 V/s ramp, closed-form kS/kV least squares
PumpkinCharacterization.wheelRadius(drive)      // slew-limited 0.25 rad/s spin;
                                                // r = (gyroDelta * driveBaseRadius) / wheelDelta
PumpkinCharacterization.rotationalInertia(drive) // spin-up torque vs alpha -> MOI estimate
PumpkinCharacterization.wheelCof(drive)          // ramp accel until slip detected (wheel vs gyro/vision)
// each returns a Command; on finish:
PumpkinConfig.writePathPlannerSettings(result);  // patches deploy/pathplanner/settings.json
PumpkinConfig.writeChoreoProject(result);        // patches the .chor robot config block
PumpkinConfig.assertConsistent();                // fails startup if TunerConstants, settings.json,
                                                 // and the .chor disagree beyond tolerance
capabilities.prerequisites: Drive subsystem SPI exposing runCharacterization(double volts), getFFCharacterizationVelocity(), getWheelRadiusCharacterizationPositions(); file write access to src/main/deploy at dev time (roboRIO deploy dir is read-only at runtime — write to /home/lvuser and provide a pull-back Gradle task). RobotConfig.hasValidConfig() exists and should be used as the runtime guard.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinNav — pathfinding facade with AdvantageKit-safe pathfinder, navgrid profiles, and warmup
capabilities.whyItMatters: Pathfinding is PathPlanner's exclusive capability and the #1 source of silent AdvantageKit replay divergence; it also has a documented cold-start JIT stall. 254 additionally swaps navgrids per phase (auto vs teleop vs backoff), which is undocumented anywhere. Three lines of config should give a team correct, replay-safe, warmed-up pathfinding with named obstacle profiles.
capabilities.prerequisites: PathPlannerLib on the classpath; AdvantageKit detected reflectively so the dependency stays optional. UNVERIFIED: whether PathPlannerLib 2026 exposes a public API to hot-swap navgrid files — 254 achieved multi-navgrid by vendoring the library, so PumpkinLib may need to ship its own Pathfinder implementation reading a selected grid.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinDrive output adapter — DriveFeedforwards/SwerveSample forces -> Phoenix 6 / REV / generic, plus setpoint generator
capabilities.whyItMatters: Both planners now emit per-module wheel forces and both are wasted unless the drive consumes them; Phoenix 6 takes them as newton arrays on ApplyRobotSpeeds. Separately, jerk-limited module control (254's setpoint generator, now shipped inside PathPlannerLib as SwerveSetpointGenerator) is what stops modules skidding and destroying odometry mid-auto. Wiring both correctly is ~40 lines a small team will get wrong.
capabilities.prerequisites: RobotConfig (from PathPlanner settings.json) is required to construct SwerveSetpointGenerator even for Choreo-only teams — PumpkinLib should be able to synthesize a RobotConfig from characterization results so Choreo-only users are not forced to open PathPlanner.

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAuto mirroring/flipping policy — one flag, correct for both symmetry types
capabilities.whyItMatters: 2910 shipped duplicate BLUE_*/RED_* .traj files, doubling regeneration work; this is the most common small-team time sink. Both libraries now support runtime transforms (PathPlannerAuto(String, boolean mirror), PathPlannerPath.flipPath()/mirrorPath(), Choreo AutoTrajectory.mirrorX()/mirrorY()/rotateAround(), AutoFactory useAllianceFlipping flag) but with different semantics and different meanings of "flip" vs "mirror". Unifying them behind one field-symmetry declaration removes an entire class of red-alliance-only bugs.
capabilities.prerequisites: Field symmetry constant per season; Choreo 2026.0.3+ for mirrorX/mirrorY/rotateAround; PathPlannerLib 2026 for PathPlannerAuto(String, boolean).

capabilities.capability: PumpkinAuto observability — per-step timeline logged to WPILog/AdvantageKit and rendered in AdvantageScope
capabilities.whyItMatters: Elite teams debug autos from logs, not from watching. PathPlanner already offers PathPlannerLogging callbacks and Choreo takes a TrajectoryLogger in the AutoFactory constructor, but neither logs step-level intent (which step, planned vs actual duration, why it exited). Making the auto structure itself observable is what turns one practice run into a diagnosis.
capabilities.prerequisites: A logging SPI so AdvantageKit is optional (fall back to WPILib DataLogManager/epilogue). Coordinate with PumpkinLib's logging/replay module.

eliteTeamPractices: Do not let the path library own the auto structure. 6328's 2026 code loads Choreo Trajectory<SwerveSample> but follows it with its own DriveTrajectory command (x/y PIDController + theta PIDController with continuous input, plus the sample's velocity feedforward, sampled via trajectory.sampleAt(timer.get(), shouldFlip())), and composes autos in Java from AutoCommands factories rather than from .auto files. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/commands/DriveTrajectory.java

Time mechanism actions against POSE, not against wall-clock. 6328's 2026 AutoCommands repeatedly uses .raceWith(Commands.sequence(Commands.waitUntil(() -> withinTolerance(Launch.leftBump, 0.25, rot)), index(...).withTimeout(launchTime))) — the launch sequence starts when the robot is physically within 0.25 m of the launch pose, not at t+X. Choreo's atTranslation(String eventName, double tol) and atPose(...) and PathPlanner's nearFieldPositionAutoFlipped / distanceFromEvent exist for exactly this. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/commands/auto/AutoCommands.java

"Start the intake 0.3s before arrival" is a first-class primitive, not a hack: Choreo AutoTrajectory.atTimeBeforeEnd(double timeBeforeEnd) and PathPlannerAuto.beforeEvent(String eventName, double timeSeconds) / distanceFromEventEnd(String, Distance). https://choreo.autos/api/choreolib/java/choreo/auto/AutoTrajectory.html and https://pathplanner.dev/api/java/com/pathplanner/lib/commands/PathPlannerAuto.html

Branch on game state, not on a fixed sequence. Choreo's own documented branching auto uses Trigger atM1 = C2toM1.done(); atM1.and(shooter::noGamepiece).onTrue(M1toM2.cmd()); atM1.and(shooter::hasGamepiece).onTrue(M1toScore.cmd()); plus routine.anyDone(scoreToM2, M1toM2) to merge converging branches. https://choreo.autos/choreolib/auto-factory/

Fully dynamic autos generated from a dashboard string. 254's 2025 AutoModeSelector exposes only DO_NOTHING and CUSTOM; CUSTOM reads startPos, iceCreamCnt, feederStrategy, and a scoringSequence/levelSequence string from NetworkTables, and PathfindingAuto walks the string calling AutoFactory.getPathfindToReefCommand(...) per character — no pre-planned paths at all. https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2025/auto/AutoModeSelector.java

Retry-on-failure and hard timing budgets are coded, not hoped for. 254's PathfindingAuto: on failed coral acquisition it does Commands.waitSeconds(1.5).andThen(Commands.waitUntil(() -> coralStateTracker.getCurrentPosition() == CoralPosition.NONE && stateMachine.getCurrentState() == SuperstructureState.STOW_CORAL)).andThen(runOnce(() -> { currentStep--; retrying = true; })); and past 12.0 s of auto it jumps currentStep forward to the next '*' in the level sequence. https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2025/auto/PathfindingAuto.java

Superstructure is a single asynchronous request target with a legality graph, not N subsystems grabbed by command groups. 254 ships SuperstructureStateMachine + a generic AStarSolver<N>.solve(N start, N goal, Heuristic<N>, Neighbors<N>) that finds a minimum-cost chain of legal transitions between superstructure states, and drives it from autos via ModalSuperstructureTriggers.setFutureStateAndWaitUntilDesiredCommand(SuperstructureState.STAGE_BARGE, ...). https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2025/subsystems/superstructure/AStarSolver.java

Control the mechanism's point, not the robot's center, when aligning. 254 vendored PathPlannerLib to add PPHolonomicDriveController.setControlPoint(Transform2d) and wraps reef approaches in setControlPoint(kDriveToCoralOffset) ... .finallyDo(() -> setControlPoint(Transform2d.kZero)). https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/com/team254/frc2025/factories/AutoFactory.java

Multiple navgrids swapped by phase. 254 ships navgrid.json, auto_navgrid.json, and backoff_navgrid.json and calls Pathfinding.setBackoffObstacles() / Pathfinding.setTeleopObstacles() around maneuvers, so the obstacle set matches the intent (tight in auto, permissive when backing off). https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public

Dependent auto questions instead of a flat 40-entry chooser. 6328's AutoSelector.addRoutine(String name, List<AutoQuestion> questions, Command command) with record AutoQuestion(String question, List<AutoQuestionResponse> responses) publishes up to 6 dropdowns per routine to NetworkTables and freezes responses once autonomous is enabled so nothing changes mid-match. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/AutoSelector.java

One class per auto, with a shared base that supplies mirroring and safety. 1678's 2026 code has AutoModeBase (wrapping factory.newRoutine(name), re-exposing trajectory(String)/trajectory(String,int)/prepRoutine(Command...)/asCommand(), and adding midline mirroring, collision detection, bump traversal with pitch monitoring, vision pose correction) with concrete modes like autos/midline/single/LeftSingleSweep. https://github.com/frc1678/C2026-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/frc/robot/autos/AutoModeBase.java

Global event-marker binding for the handful of universally-safe actions, Java triggers for everything else. 1678's AutoHelpers.bindEventMarkers() binds only "intake", "spinUp" (1900 RPM, 19.5 deg hood) and "expandHopper" via factory.bind(); everything conditional lives in Java. https://github.com/frc1678/C2026-Public/blob/main/src/main/java/frc/robot/autos/AutoHelpers.java

Score/shoot on the move by overriding only the rotation channel of the trajectory follower. 6328's DriveTrajectory takes Supplier<Optional<Double>> omegaOverride and AutoCommands.followTrajectoryWhileAiming(name, drive, start, shouldAim, mirror) passes () -> shouldAim.getAsBoolean() ? Optional.of(launchOnTheMoveOmega()) : Optional.empty(). PathPlanner's equivalent is PPHolonomicDriveController.overrideRotationFeedback(DoubleSupplier) (setRotationTargetOverride is deprecated). https://pathplanner.dev/api/java/com/pathplanner/lib/controllers/PPHolonomicDriveController.html

Use opponent/game-piece vision to reshape the auto plan at runtime. 6328's 2026 AutoCommands.getDynamicBounds(...) reads ObjectDetection.getInstance().getRobotTranslations() and expands the search region when adjacent quadrants are unoccupied, and a SalesmanSolver (TSP) orders the pickup sequence over detected game pieces. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/commands/auto/AutoCommands.java

Blend the profile feedforward out near the goal during pose alignment. 6328's DriveToPose scales linear and theta feedforward by clamp((error - ffMin)/(ffMax - ffMin), 0, 1) so the trapezoid FF does not overshoot at close range, with ~14 LoggedTunableNumbers and a withinTolerance(double driveTolerance, Rotation2d thetaTolerance) query. https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/commands/DriveToPose.java

Measure, don't guess, the config that drives trajectory generation. 6328's DriveCommands.feedforwardCharacterization does a 0.1 V/s ramp after a 2 s settle and fits kS/kV with a closed-form least-squares; wheelRadiusCharacterization spins at SlewRateLimiter(0.05)-limited 0.25 rad/s and computes wheelRadius = (gyroDelta * driveBaseRadius) / wheelDelta. The AdvantageKit TalonFX swerve template documents both as selectable autonomous routines with console output copied into TunerConstants.java. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/template-projects/talonfx-swerve-template/

Simulate the auto against the game, not just the drivetrain. 6328's 2026 SimTrajectory(String name, FuelSim fuelSim, int instance, BooleanSupplier isBlueAlliance, BooleanSupplier mirror) replays a Choreo trajectory against a fuel simulation, recording setpoint poses, velocities, and fuel collected — i.e. they score candidate autos offline. maple-sim provides the equivalent physics/game-piece layer as an open-source library. https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/swerve-simulation-overview/

Preload everything at startup. Both libraries warn that trajectory/auto loading is blocking and can consume seconds of match time on the RIO; PathPlanner adds FollowPathCommand.warmupCommand() and Choreo 2026.0.3 added a Java warmup command specifically to force JIT before autonomous. https://choreo.autos/choreolib/trajectory-api/ and https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-follow-a-single-path.html

Keep pathfinding deterministic under replay. AdvantageKit users must call Pathfinding.setPathfinder(new LocalADStarAK()) before warmup or log replay diverges; PathPlanner's own docs point at the LocalADStarAK gist. https://gist.github.com/mjansen4857/a8024b55eb427184dbd10ae8923bd57d
pitfalls: PathPlanner NamedCommands that share subsystem requirements with the auto command group will CANCEL the auto group when triggered. This is documented explicitly for Event Triggers and is the most common "my auto stops halfway" bug. The fix is a superstructure request bus that owns mechanism requirements once, with event markers only firing requests. https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-triggers.html

Choreo trajectories cannot be regenerated to match the robot's actual starting linear velocity or rotation — PathPlanner's docs call this out as the key limitation of fromChoreoTrajectory. If your robot starts 10 cm off, the feedforward is wrong from sample 0. Mitigation: always resetOdometry from the trajectory's initial pose (or trust vision), and prefer PathPlanner regeneration for the first path of an auto if start-pose repeatability is poor. https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-choreo-interop.html

Choreo does not support PathPlanner-style zoned events — Choreo markers are instants only. Any design that assumes "whileTrue over a zone" must synthesize it (atTime start + atTime end, or atTranslation entry/exit). https://choreo.autos/usage/editing-paths/

Loading trajectories or autos during autonomous is a blocking operation that can take multiple seconds on a roboRIO. Both projects tell you to load at startup. A PumpkinLib API that lazily loads on first use (Choreo AutoChooser.addRoutine's Supplier) must still force-warm every registered variant at robotInit or you trade a chooser convenience for lost match time. https://choreo.autos/choreolib/trajectory-api/

AdvantageKit log replay silently diverges if PathPlanner's default LocalADStar pathfinder is used, because pathfinding runs on a background thread with non-deterministic timing. Must use LocalADStarAK. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/common-issues/non-deterministic-data-sources/

Cold-start JIT: the first pathfind or path-follow after boot can stall long enough to matter. PathPlanner ships FollowPathCommand.warmupCommand() and Choreo 2026.0.3 added a warmup command explicitly because "eliminating autonomous delays" required preloading classes at robot startup. https://github.com/SleipnirGroup/Choreo/releases

Three separate sources of truth for the same physical constants: TunerConstants.java (Phoenix 6), deploy/pathplanner/settings.json (consumed by RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()), and the .chor project's robot config. When they drift, trajectory generation is silently wrong. RobotConfig.hasValidConfig() exists to check against GUI settings and should be asserted at startup. https://pathplanner.dev/api/java/com/pathplanner/lib/config/RobotConfig.html

SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds does NOT discretize chassis speeds — the caller must call ChassisSpeeds.discretize. Forgetting this produces a persistent skew/drift during path following that looks like a bad odometry calibration. Also ApplyChassisSpeeds is deprecated for removal in 2026 in favor of ApplyRobotSpeeds. https://api.ctr-electronics.com/phoenix6/stable/java/com/ctre/phoenix6/swerve/SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds.html

Wheel force feedforward arrays must be ordered to match the SwerveDrivetrain's module order, in newtons. Getting the order wrong is not an error — it just makes the robot fight itself under acceleration. https://api.ctr-electronics.com/phoenix6/stable/java/com/ctre/phoenix6/swerve/SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds.html

PPHolonomicDriveController's feedback overrides are STATIC (overrideXFeedback, overrideRotationFeedback, clearFeedbackOverrides). Anything that sets them must clear them in finallyDo, or the override leaks into the next command — 254 uses exactly this .finallyDo discipline for setControlPoint. Static global state in a path follower is a real hazard for a library trying to be composable. https://pathplanner.dev/api/java/com/pathplanner/lib/controllers/PPHolonomicDriveController.html

AD* is an anytime algorithm: it publishes progressively refined solutions in the background, so the robot can visibly change direction mid-motion. This surprises teams who expect a single committed path. It also means pathfinding results are not reproducible run to run. https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-pathfinding.html

navgrid.json must exist in deploy/pathplanner for pathfinding; it is created automatically only when the project is opened in the PathPlanner GUI. A Choreo-primary team that never opens PathPlanner will have pathfinding fail at the event. https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-pathfinding.html

Wheel radius characterization on a hard floor gives a wrong answer — the AdvantageKit template explicitly says to run it on carpet. Since wheel radius feeds odometry scale, path length, and PathPlanner's module config, this one measurement error corrupts everything downstream. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/template-projects/talonfx-swerve-template/

Duplicating alliance-specific trajectory files (2910's BLUE_*/RED_* .traj set) doubles regeneration cost and guarantees the two sets drift. Both libraries now support runtime transforms: PathPlannerAuto(String, boolean mirror), PathPlannerPath.flipPath()/mirrorPath(), Choreo AutoTrajectory.mirrorX()/mirrorY()/rotateAround() (added 2026.0.3) and AutoFactory's useAllianceFlipping flag. Note flip (rotational symmetry) and mirror (reflective symmetry) are different operations — picking the wrong one for the season's field is a red-alliance-only bug that never shows up in practice on blue. https://github.com/SleipnirGroup/Choreo/releases

PathPlanner's origin stays on the blue side even when paths are flipped — shouldFlipPath transforms path coordinates only, not the coordinate frame. Mixing this with a vision system that reports alliance-relative poses produces a hard-to-find offset. https://pathplanner.dev/pplib-build-an-auto.html

Choreo Empty waypoints cannot be trajectory endpoints, and constraint scoping (waypoint vs segment vs both) is easy to get wrong in a way that produces a solvable-but-slow or infeasible problem. Optimizer failures are opaque; 2026.0.3 added a fallback routine for line search failures, which implies these failures are common. https://choreo.autos/usage/editing-paths/

WPILib 2027 will break every auto codebase: packages move edu.wpi.first -> org.wpilib, Java 25 is required, Commands v2 loses controller-based commands and RamseteCommand, Commands v3 (coroutines) arrives, Shuffleboard AND SmartDashboard are removed (so SendableChooser-on-SmartDashboard auto selection dies), PathWeaver is removed with Choreo named as successor, and every 2026 project must be re-imported. Any PumpkinLib auto API that leaks WPILib command types into user signatures will force a user-code rewrite; leak PumpkinLib types instead. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

Systemcore (2027) changes the hardware substrate entirely — multiple CAN buses, onboard IMU, and removal of Relay/analog output/SPI/DMA. Any PumpkinLib auto feature that assumes roboRIO CPU budget (e.g. on-robot trajectory optimization) should be validated against Systemcore before committing. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

PathPlannerLib 2025+ has no replanning: AutoBuilder.configure takes no ReplanningConfig parameter and none appears in the current RobotConfig/AutoBuilder API. Teams migrating from 2024 code or copying 2024 tutorials will look for it and find stale advice. UNVERIFIED: the exact release note announcing removal was not located, but its absence from the 2026 API is verified. https://pathplanner.dev/api/java/com/pathplanner/lib/auto/AutoBuilder.html

Testing dozens of auto variants only in the PathPlanner/Choreo GUI validates geometry, not mechanism timing or game-piece acquisition. Nothing off-the-shelf asserts "this auto finishes in 15 s and scores 3"; without a headless harness, variant N+1 is validated by hope. maple-sim provides the physics but no assertion layer. https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/

Choreo's AutoRoutine is polled on its own EventLoop — external Triggers used inside a routine must be wrapped with routine.observe(BooleanSupplier) or they will be evaluated on the default loop and fire outside the routine's lifetime. https://choreo.autos/api/choreolib/java/choreo/auto/AutoRoutine.html
